scenario: Documentary-film scholars study films that are still discussed on the festival circuit, observing a mean critical-score of 6.8 out of 10 (σ=1.5). The recall threshold is 4.5 (minimum score to remain in festival circulation). The true mean quality across all documentaries produced is unknown.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming critical score is normally distributed with σ=1.5 score points, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>4.5]=6.8. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The documentary films remembered after festival circuit critical score set is a truncated-normal sample above the 4.5 threshold. Solving E[X|X>4.5]=μ+σφ((4.5−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((4.5−μ)/σ)=6.8 gives μ≈6.5401. Only 91.3% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 0.2599 score points.

naive_answer: The true mean critical score is 6.8 score points because that is the observed average among documentary films remembered after festival circuit.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=4.5. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=6.8. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈6.5401. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((4.5−6.5401)/σ)≈0.9131.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 6.8,1.5,4.5
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-6.5401)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.9131)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
